points.quote: The desktop file adds `electron-browser/desktop.main.js` and `desktop.contribution.js`. It also adds native services such as `nativeTextFileService`, `nativeHostService`, `lifecycleService` and the native `fileDialogService`.
The web file adds `browser/web.main.js`. It also adds browser services such as `browserTextFileService`, the browser `extensionService` and `webExtensionsScannerService`.
`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` imports the platform-neutral workbench. ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` and `workbench.web.main.ts` each start with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`.
Both builds register the same service interfaces, such as text files and extensions. Each one registers a different implementation.
A module only loads if a reachable entry file imports it, directly or through a barrel.
Each contribution registers itself on import through side effects such as `registerSingleton`, `registerWorkbenchContribution2` and action registration.
